identity.title: Solar Chromospheric Temperature Diagnostics: A Joint ALMA-Hα Analysis

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the first high-resolution, simultaneous observations of the solar chromosphere in the optical and millimeter wavelength ranges, obtained with ALMA and the IBIS instrument at the Dunn Solar Telescope.

targets.name: Plage, network and fibrils in NOAA AR 12651

evidence.quote: The center of the target region was at E04, N11 at the time of the observations ($\mu = 0.96$ or heliocentric angle of 16$^{\circ}$).
The center of the target region was at E04, N11 at the time of the observations ($\mu = 0.96$ or heliocentric angle of 16$^{\circ}$).

question.value: How does the ALMA Band 3 brightness temperature relate to the H-alpha core width as a chromospheric temperature diagnostic, and what physical mechanism explains the relation?

evidence.quote: we concentrate on the comparison between the brightness temperature observed in ALMA Band 3 (3 mm; 100 GHz) and the core width of the H$\alpha$ 6563 Å line
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/NRAO.ALMA#2016.1.01129.S.
The data analyzed here were obtained in Band 3 (2.8-3.3 mm, 92-108 GHz) in the interval 17:19 to 18:53 UT.
180 interleaved scans of H$\alpha$ 6563, Ca II 8542, and Na I D1 5896 Å

configurations.value: C40-3, max baseline 460 m nominal, 396 m actual

evidence.quote: The ALMA data were obtained with the array in configuration C40-3 with a maximum baseline of 460 m. However, due to antenna issues, during these observations the maximum baseline was 396 m.
the restoring beam size of the ALMA image, as calculated in CLEAN, is 1.75$''$ x 1.91$''$ in the x-y directions

time_on_source.value: eight intervals of ~593 s on target with 145 s phase calibrator gaps

evidence.quote: dwelled for approximately 593 seconds on the target followed by a 145 second gap for observations of a phase calibrator.
We obtained a coordinated set of observations between ALMA and the Dunn Solar Telescope (cite: 1991AdSpR..11..139D) on April 23, 2017.

analysis_steps.goal: Calibrate and self-calibrate ALMA data, feather with full-disk

method.value: Standard CASA calibration, per-interval self-calibration, feathering with single-dish, normalised to 7300 K

evidence.quote: we apply a self-calibration technique.

method.value: Width of line profile at half line depth, with depth defined relative to intensity at ±1.0 Å

evidence.quote: we measure the separation of the line profile wings at half of the line depth, defined as the difference between the line minimum and the intensity at $\pm$ 1.0 Å from the core position

fitting.value: second-order polynomial to line core for minimum

evidence.quote: were determined through fitting of a second-order polynomial to the line core
the errors in the line width were determined to be about 0.005 Å

method.value: Convolve IBIS with elliptical Gaussian 1.95'' x 2.03'', bin ALMA in time by 8 maps, align, 2D histogram, Pearson r and orthogonal distance regression

evidence.quote: Because of the scatter present in both measurements, we perform an orthogonal distance regression (cite: 1990ApJ...364..104I) to find the best linear fit between the two parameters.

method.value: Synthesize H-alpha and 3 mm intensity from SRPM and VAL C models with 4-level hydrogen with PRD for Ly-alpha, Ly-beta, H-alpha; compare to observed correlation

evidence.quote: The RH calculations were done using a 4-level (including continuum) hydrogen atom with the Ly-alpha, Ly-beta and Balmer-alpha transitions treated under partial redistribution (PRD)

assumptions.value: 1D hydrostatic semi-empirical atmospheres; mm radiation in Rayleigh-Jeans approximation

evidence.quote: The emergent millimetric radiation was calculated from the synthetic intensity under the Rayleigh-Jeans approximation

validation.value: model points compared with observed correlation

evidence.quote: coincide well with the observational data for models B to P

findings_qualitative.value: Bright fibril-like structures are seen in on-disk ALMA images, contrary to Rutten (2017) prediction of dark fibrils

evidence.quote: we identify them as bright (hence hot) features, rather than dark, strong fibrils

claims.hypothesis: Is ALMA 3 mm T_B correlated with H-alpha core width?
claims.finding: Strong correlation; width is a temperature proxy over 6500-12000 K

evidence.quote: The correlation is very strong across the full range in temperature present in our FOV

claims.hypothesis: Is H-alpha width broadening thermal Doppler?
claims.experiment: Compare ALMA T range with width variation

evidence.quote: is only about 0.025 Å, an order of magnitude smaller than the observed variation of 0.3 Å

claims.hypothesis: A shared dependence on n=2 hydrogen population drives the correlation
claims.result: Models B to P reproduce the trend; n2 rises with hotter models
claims.finding: Both diagnostics depend on n2 via Ly-alpha flux

evidence.quote: We hypothesize that the underlying physical mechanism for the correlation
